set.body:
Objective

Turn the certified fixed-bilinear foundation into one statistically valid and brain-scale-qualified workflow:

raw fMRI -> relation_fit -> residual sufficient statistics -> provenance-frozen metric recipe -> executable evidence plan -> query-first local crossnobis map.

Constitution

The universal evaluator remains E(H,K) = tr(H^T B_L K B_R^T). A relation remains the pure experimental-neural map. relation_fit composes that signal with an error capability. Metrics and bridges are role-distinct. Learned matrices are derived on demand from frozen recipes and stable source revisions, never stored as a searchlight-by-fold table.

Critical constraints

- The additive WA collapse is available only when the compiled metric is feature-additive in the native basis.
- Dense local metrics use a support-streamed lowering; no p-by-p, m-by-p-squared, m-by-k-squared, or m-by-edge-by-k-squared persistent object is permitted.
- Every public request executes the canonical plan from which its receipt is derived.
- Coherent/configuration components include the metric and coherent functional in their identity.
- Point-estimate metric construction and uncertainty calibration remain separate but share provenance.

Program acceptance

One raw-response simulation reaches a signed local crossnobis map; known-metric and learned-metric paths agree with independent oracles; null and planted effects behave as declared; query-first and small full materialization agree; operator-learning provenance prevents undeclared evaluation-data access; a declared 50-60k-feature gate either passes or narrows the supported metric regime honestly; and every exported workflow is executable at its declared scale.

Deferred

Classifier accuracy, classifier registries, population inference, generic plugins, all-pairs brain connectivity, dense tomography, arbitrary nonlinear edge pipelines, and new theoretical specification documents remain out of scope until this slice passes.
set.title: Epic: Statistical and brain-scale realization of evidence pairing
